question: How to realize Topology Optimization of Cavity-Based Second Harmonic Generation?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer must define the method as large-scale topology optimization in which every pixel of the cavity geometry is a degree of freedom—thousands of free parameters determined entirely by computational search, with little or no a priori design information.
examples: every pixel of the geometry is a design degree of freedom
computational search with thousands of free parameters replaces hand-designed cavities
the structure is found by computational search rather than design heuristics

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer must state that the core objective is maximizing the nonlinear overlap integral β̄ between the fundamental field E1 and the harmonic field E2—not merely maximizing individual Purcell factors or mode volumes, which is insufficient for SHG.
examples: the key is to maximize the special overlap integral β̄ between E1 and E2
the overlap integral, not the individual Purcell factors, determines SHG
optimizing mode volumes of single resonances is insufficient

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer must require two strongly coupled modes at ω1 (infrared) and ω2 = 2ω1 (visible), with frequency matching between the resonances and small confinement factors for both modes.
examples: strongly coupled fundamental and harmonic modes at ω1 and 2ω1
coupled IR pump mode and visible harmonic mode with matched frequencies
frequency matching plus small confinement factors are enforced

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Answer must present Q1²Q2|β̄|²—the combination of both modes' quality factors with the nonlinear overlap—as the enhancement figure of merit to be maximized, noting orders-of-magnitude improvement in nonlinear coupling.
examples: maximize Q1²Q2|β̄|²
enhancement scales with the square of Q1 and the harmonic Q2
orders-of-magnitude improvement in β̄ yields large SHG enhancement

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Answer must specify that the optimized cavities support long-lived modes at both pump and harmonic frequencies with quality factors Q1, Q2 > 10⁴.
examples: quality factors exceeding 10⁴ for both modes
long-lived resonances at both infrared and visible wavelengths
large mode lifetimes for the fundamental and harmonic

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer should describe the frequency-averaged LDOS formulation extending single-mode optimization to multi-mode cavities: maximize the minimum of LDOS(ω1) and LDOS(2ω1) via two small scattering problems with point sources (M1E1 = J1, M2E2 = J2), enabling scalable adjoint-based gradients.
examples: max min[LDOS(ω1), LDOS(2ω1)]
two point sources at ω1 and 2ω1 drive two scattering calculations
frequency-averaged LDOS converts cavity optimization into a series of small scattering problems

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer should contrast the approach with prior designs based on known linear cavity structures hand-tailored to maximize Purcell factors of individual resonances (ring resonators, nanobeam cavities), which ensure neither overlap nor frequency matching.
examples: unlike hand-tailored ring resonators or nanobeam cavities
prior work maximizes Purcell factors of individual resonances rather than the nonlinear overlap
computational search offers a route where heuristics fail

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer should mention the novel multilayer micropost and grating microcavity designs obtained as experimentally feasible demonstrations, and that the framework lays the groundwork for topology optimization of 2D/3D slab structures with further improvements.
examples: novel micropost and grating microcavity designs with Q > 10⁴ coupled IR and visible modes
multilayer-stack optimization in an experimentally feasible setting
extension to 2D/3D slab structures is the expected next step
